statement: A park lawn is made of a rectangle that is $100$ meters long and $60$ meters wide, with a semicircle attached along each of the two $60$-meter sides. Each semicircle has that $60$-meter side as its diameter. Which expression gives the total area of the lawn, in square meters?

choices.misconception: I found the area of one semicircle, $450\pi$, and forgot that there is a semicircle on each end.
I treated each end as a full circle of radius 30, so I added $2 \times 900\pi = 1{,}800\pi$.
I used 60 as the radius instead of the diameter, so the two semicircles became one circle with area $\pi(60)^2 = 3{,}600\pi$.

hints: Two semicircles with the same diameter make one full circle.
Add the area of the rectangle to the area of one circle whose diameter is $60$ meters.
The rectangle has area $100 \times 60 = 6{,}000$, and the circle has radius $30$, so its area is $\pi(30)^2$.

solutions.reliable: The rectangle has area $100 \times 60 = 6{,}000$ square meters. Each semicircle has diameter $60$, so radius $30$, and area $\frac{1}{2}\pi(30)^2 = 450\pi$. The two semicircles together have area $900\pi$. The total area is $6{,}000 + 900\pi$ square meters.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
